status: Focused primary-source comparison, not exhaustive priority certification

comparisons.inspection: Primary PDF model, algorithm loop, Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.4 inspected
comparisons.finding: Derived dyadic corollary: take k proportional to N^(2alpha), fixed epsilon, delta proportional to N^(-alpha-1/2) in the paper's coordinate error theorem. Unitary normalization and ||Ux||1 <= sqrt(N)||x||2 give O(N^-alpha)||x||2 coordinate error for alpha<1/2. Recovery costs O(N^(.5+alpha) log^(3/2)N)=o(N), and paid dense input/output/root preparation makes O(N). Constant independent repetition strengthens failure N^-1 to N^-c for fixed c. Thus the weak approximate headline is not new on dyadic lengths in a compatible ideal-arithmetic model.
comparisons.boundary: This is an inference from the theorem, not its literal statement. The general-length remark mentions N/phi(N), but algorithm divisibility B|N prevents treating that remark alone as a verified arbitrary-length compiler. Root, coefficient precision and word-operation model require matching.

comparisons.inspection: Primary theorem and appendix runtime inspected
comparisons.finding: Any-universe linfty/l2 sparse recovery does not by itself establish an O(k polylog N) runtime. The inspected runtime is O(N log^3 N log k), with polynomial-SNR assumptions. It cannot be substituted into k=N^(2alpha) to claim O(N) all-length output.

comparisons.inspection: Primary theorem and word-RAM discussion independently inspected by global reviewer
comparisons.finding: Finite-field lookup-table transforms and ordinary fixed-field WHT word packing are established prior mechanisms. The cited bit bound is O(NlogN/loglogN); word-RAM and bit-permutation costs are separately discussed. This is not a theorem for rounded complex FFT with deterministic relative l2 error, so it motivates a priority search rather than proving subsumption.

comparisons.inspection: Primary author-hosted theorem/model inspected; full blocked-ring corollary read in second independent audit
comparisons.finding: Cantor-Kaltofen gives multiplication over arbitrary algebras using O(nlogn) algebra products and O(nlognloglogn) additions. Logarithmic blocking into a small truncated-polynomial ring plus charged lookup tables gives the same O(LloglogL) carryless binary convolution order as the catalogue extension. That comparison is a derived corollary; no claim the 1991 text literally states the modern word-RAM contract.

Prony/annihilating recurrence, sparse Fourier recovery and pruned synthesis are close established ingredients. Exact project claims include raw recognition, rejection accounting, supplied-root scans, dense full output and structured fiber/chirp families. No model-matched prior theorem was located that conclusively subsumes all those combined parameters; this is not priority evidence.
